xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-4499: pan handoff: --skill/--pack for the new conversation, and --hold to create it without sending the kickoff

plan.title: pan handoff: --skill/--pack for the new conversation, and --hold to create it without sending the kickoff
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

metadata.sizeJustification: One acceptance criterion (the combined `pan handoff --skill --pack --model --effort --hold` invocation, then a dashboard Send or `pan handoff start` delivering the kickoff once) spans the CLI, the server fork pipeline, a new SQLite column, a new route, and the dashboard composer; the hold is unusable without a start path and the dashboard start path is an explicit issue AC. Tests, the regenerated composer manifest, and the lockstep SKILL.md push the file count past 25 and the subsystem count (first two path segments) past 6, but every item is a small vertical slice and the files listed are mostly new leaf modules and their tests.

narratives.Problem: pan handoff cannot give the new conversation its own skills (PAN-4486's per-conversation skill layer is only writable from the new-conversation dialog; the --issue workaround leaks the skill to every agent on the issue), and it always sends the handoff document as the first message, so the operator cannot inspect a successor before it starts working.
narratives.Proposal: Add repeatable --skill and --pack to pan handoff. The server route validates them against the native and pack catalogs (400 before any row is created, listing known names) and writes them, on top of the inherited source map, into the successor's conversations.skill_overrides; --pack expands to <pack>/<skill>: true for every non-opt-in skill of the cached manifest. Add --hold: the fork pipeline authors and launches as today but stores the kickoff in a new conversations.held_kickoff column instead of sending it, finishing with forkStatus null. A new kickoff door (GET/POST /api/conversations/:name/kickoff) claims the held text atomically and delivers it once through the shared deliverForkSeed tail; pan handoff start <conv> and the dashboard composer Send both use it. The dashboard composer of a held conversation shows a waiting notice and is seeded with the kickoff; the fork modal parses --skill/--pack/--hold out of /handoff text and sends them. Docs and the pan-handoff skill describe all of it.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No change to skill resolution rules in resolve.ts or launch.ts, and no conversation-level pack toggle
- No global, project, or issue skill-override write from pan handoff
- No full skill picker in the fork modal; only parsed chips and a hold checkbox
- No new forkStatus value for held conversations
- No list badge or Command Deck row marker for held conversations
- pan tell and other delivery paths do not clear the hold
- No --hold on pan fork
- No composer execution policy for /pan handoff start (stays terminal-only)
- No edits to routes/conversations.ts (zero file-size headroom) and no allowlist raises

autoDecisions.summary: Server validates --skill/--pack; the CLI forwards skills[] and packs[] and relays the 400 message.
autoDecisions.rationale: fork-client.ts documents the summary-fork route as the single owner of the fork pipeline; validating there keeps one door and covers the dashboard fork modal too.

autoDecisions.summary: --pack expands to <pack>/<skill>: true entries for every non-opt-in skill in the cached manifest; uncached packs fail with the existing 'run pan skills pack sync' wording.
autoDecisions.rationale: The conversation layer stores per-skill values only and resolvePackSkill already honors them, so no resolver change is needed; skipping opt-in skills matches pack-toggle semantics at every other level.

autoDecisions.summary: Requested skill entries are merged on top of the source conversation's inherited skill map (requested entries win).
autoDecisions.rationale: The fork route already copies the source's launch context; the flags are a narrower request for this successor.

autoDecisions.summary: Core skills named by --skill are accepted and store nothing.
autoDecisions.rationale: Core skills are always on, so the request is already satisfied; rejecting it would be friction with no safety value.

autoDecisions.summary: The held kickoff is stored as text in a new conversations.held_kickoff column read/written by a new leaf module, not through LegacyConversation.
autoDecisions.rationale: It covers the fallback-summary case that has no handoff document file, gives an atomic SQLite claim for exactly-once, and avoids src/lib/overdeck/conversations.ts, which has 3 lines of file-size headroom.

autoDecisions.summary: A held pipeline finishes with forkStatus null; no 'held' forkStatus value.
autoDecisions.rationale: getStuckForks, recoverStuckForks, the lifecycle sweeper and the CLI's isForkResultInProgress all treat any non-null non-failed forkStatus as in flight.

autoDecisions.summary: pan handoff start is a Commander subcommand mirroring planCmd.command('finalize'), with a fallback to intercepting convRef === 'start' if Commander misroutes.
autoDecisions.rationale: Matches the existing plan/plan finalize pattern; conversation names are generated (YYYYMMDD-xxxx) so 'start' is not a real conversation reference.

autoDecisions.summary: The dashboard composer of a held conversation is seeded with the kickoff and its Send posts to the kickoff door (no text when unchanged, edited text otherwise).
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue asks for the kickoff ready in the composer with Send starting it; routing Send through the claim door makes exactly-once hold for both the dashboard and the CLI.

autoDecisions.summary: The /handoff composer pass-through is implemented by parsing --skill/--pack/--hold out of the fork modal's initialFocus.
autoDecisions.rationale: Both /handoff (frontend regex) and /pan handoff (server control plane) already deliver the trailing text to ForkModal as initialFocus, so one parser covers both with no change to the composer regex, control plane, or open-fork-modal event.

items.title: Resolve --skill/--pack requests into conversation skill-layer entries

narrative.Action: Implement PRD WI-1: new module src/lib/skill-overrides/conversation-flags.ts exporting ConversationSkillFlagError, parseSkillFlagList(raw, 'skills'|'packs'), the pure expandConversationSkillFlags(flags, catalog), and resolveConversationSkillFlags(flags, projectRoot) which loads listSkillCatalog({ projectRoot }) and listPackCatalog() then expands. Follow the PRD's ordered rules exactly: pack expansion to non-opt-in <pack>/<skill>: true, uncached pack -> 'pack <id> is not cached; run pan skills pack sync <id>', unknown pack -> 'unknown pack: <id>. Known packs: ...', unknown skill -> 'unknown skill: <name>. Known skills: ...' (native names then cached pack skill ids, sorted), core skills accepted with no entry. Write the seven named tests with in-memory catalogs.

items.title: Given a cached pack with two non-opt-in skills and one opt-in skill, expandConversationSkillFlags({ packs: ['p'] }) returns exactly the two non-opt-in <pack>/<skill>: true entries

An unknown pack throws ConversationSkillFlagError whose message starts 'unknown pack: nope. Known packs:' and lists the registered pack ids; an uncached pack throws the 'run pan skills pack sync' message
An unknown skill name or unknown <pack>/<skill> id throws a message starting 'unknown skill: <name>. Known skills:' that lists native names and cached pack skill ids
A core skill name (e.g. pan-done) is accepted and produces no entry; parseSkillFlagList rejects a non-array or a malformed id with 'Invalid skills'/'Invalid packs'
Fork route writes requested skills and packs on the successor's row

narrative.Action: Implement PRD WI-4: add the single line `/** PAN-4499: launch without sending the kickoff. */ hold?: boolean;` to ForkRequest in src/lib/overdeck/conversations.ts; in conversation-forks.ts add hold to buildForkRequest, extract the exported deliverForkSeed(conv, seed, caller) from runForkPipeline's tail (calling self.injectForkSummary so existing spies keep working), add a last runForkPipeline parameter hold = false whose branch calls holdKickoff, markConversationActive and updateForkStatus(null) after ensureForkSessionReady, pass request.hold === true in recoverStuckForks, parse body.hold === true in handleConversationSummaryFork, reject hold with forkMode plain (400 'hold is not supported for plain forks'), and pass hold into buildForkRequest and runForkPipeline. narrative.Action: Implement PRD WI-5: new src/lib/overdeck/conversation-kickoff.ts with startHeldKickoff(name, text?) returning started/not-found/not-held/invalid (text optional; when given it must be a string of 1-100000 trimmed chars), which claims with claimHeldKickoff and starts deliverClaimedKickoff in the background via registerInFlightForkPipeline; deliverClaimedKickoff calls ensureForkSessionReady(conv, conv.claudeSessionId, false) then deliverForkSeed(conv, seed, 'handoff-kickoff'), and on a throw from either restores the hold and sets forkStatus 'failed' (never markConversationEnded). New top-level route file src/dashboard/server/routes/conversation-kickoff.ts with GET (404 / {held:true,text} / {held:false}) and POST (200 {success, conversation} / 404 / 409 'No held kickoff: the conversation was already started or was never held' / 400), following postConversationSummaryForkRoute's origin check and body reading; register conversationKickoffRouteLayer in server.ts next to conversationsRouteLayer; add the two no-loss-matrix rows and the two route-scopes rows (GET read:conversations, POST tell). Write the five named route tests.

items.title: GET /api/conversations/:name/kickoff returns { held: true, text } for a held conversation, { held: false } after it is started, and 404 for an unknown name
